subject: Logic
title: Classification of Finite Groups
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Classification of Finite Groups.

hook.text: Imagine cataloging every type of symmetry in the universe. Mathematicians did exactly that—it took 100 years.

buildup.text: The classification theorem lists all finite simple groups—the atoms of symmetry in mathematics.

discovery.text: The proof spans over 10,000 pages across hundreds of journal articles by dozens of mathematicians.

twist.text: The strangest entry: the Monster group, with more elements than atoms in the Earth. It exists but defies imagination.

climax.text: It's the longest proof in history—so long that verifying it is itself a decades-long project.

punchline.text: Every symmetry, cataloged. Ten thousand pages.

quiz.question: What does the classification of finite simple groups achieve?
options: Catalogs every type of finite simple group
